unit.title: Attend to break downs in hazardous areas

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A maintenance fitter is called to a leaking pump seal in a fuel depot's pump bay. Why is this bay treated as a hazardous area?
options: The pumps are heavy and very hard to lift out
Fuel vapour may mix with air and could ignite
The floor is often wet and slippery
The noise level is above the safe limit

questions.stem: On a hazardous area drawing, what does 'Zone 0' mean?
options: No hazard; work freely there
Gas may be present only after a very large leak
Gas is present now and then in normal work
An explosive mix is there all or most of the time

questions.stem: Of the three zones used for gases, which one is usually the least hazardous?
options: Zone 2
Zone 0
Zone 1
Zone 20

questions.stem: At a sugar factory, fine sugar dust collects on the beams in the bagging area. Why does this matter to a fitter doing a breakdown there?
options: Sugar dust makes the floor sticky
Sugar dust blocks the welding fumes
A dust cloud can explode if it is ignited
Sugar dust makes the steel rust very quickly

questions.stem: The zone of the pump bay is not marked on site. What should the team leader do before planning the repair?
options: Check the site's area classification drawing
Assume it is safe since no sign is up
Ask the truck drivers what they think
Sniff the air near the pump to see if fuel is there

questions.stem: A pipe support at an LPG bottling plant has broken. Who may carry out the repair?
options: Any fitter from the shop who is free that day
Authorised people working under a permit
The plant's security guard
Any welder with his own machine

questions.stem: Which set of details belongs on a permit for hot work in a hazardous area?
options: The welder's pay rate and overtime
The client's bank details and invoice number
The weather forecast for the week
The work, isolations, gas tests and time limits

questions.stem: Gas testing for a weld repair at a fuel depot showed a safe reading at 8 a.m. Welding will last all day. What should happen?
options: No more tests are needed today
Test again only if someone smells fuel nearby
Keep testing during the work, as the permit says
Test once more at the end of the day

questions.stem: LPG is heavier than air. Where must the gas tester check most carefully before hot work at an LPG plant?
options: At roof level, where the gas will rise to
Only at the welder's head height
Upwind of the work, in the open
Low down: drains, pits and trenches

questions.stem: A detector reads 0% LEL at the start of a weld repair, then the reading rises to 15% LEL. What should the team do?
options: Stop hot work, make safe and find the leak
Carry on, as 15% is a low number
Weld faster, to finish before it rises any more
Open the oxygen valve to dilute it

questions.stem: A helper suggests cracking open an oxygen cylinder into a pit to 'sweeten the air' before the welder goes in. Why is this dangerous?
options: Oxygen is too cold and causes frostbite
Oxygen is heavier than fuel gas
Extra oxygen makes things burn fiercely
Oxygen sets off the gas detector alarm

questions.stem: Which check shows that a portable gas detector is fit to use on the day?
options: It switches on and the screen lights up brightly
A bump test with test gas, and calibration in date
It has been charged overnight
It reads zero in the workshop

questions.stem: A leaking valve on a fuel line must be replaced. Besides electrical isolation of the pump, what is needed?
options: Process isolation: closed, drained and purged
Only a sign saying 'Do not use'
Tape wrapped round the valve handle and the pipe
A bucket under the leak

questions.stem: Why is a spade (blind) fitted between flanges often preferred to relying on one closed valve?
options: It is far cheaper than buying a new valve
It lets fuel through more slowly
It needs no permit to fit
A valve can leak; a blind is a positive break

questions.stem: A pipe has been purged with nitrogen before a weld repair. What new hazard must the team control?
options: The pipe becomes too hot to touch
Nitrogen can suffocate people in low spaces
Nitrogen makes the weld metal brittle and weak
Nitrogen is highly flammable

questions.stem: A small crack is found in a fuel pipe in a Zone 1 area. Which repair approach should be considered first?
options: Weld it at once, while the line is still running
Wrap it in tape and leave it
A cold method, such as a bolted clamp, if approved
Braze it with a gas torch

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of ignition that a fitter could bring into a hazardous area?
options: A paper permit
A steel tape measure
A cotton rag
An angle grinder

questions.stem: A fitter wants to photograph a broken bracket inside a Zone 1 area for his report. What should he use?
options: Only a camera certified for that zone
His own phone, as long as the flash is off
Any phone, if he is quick
A tablet in a plastic bag

questions.stem: Fuel is drained from a pump into a portable container before a repair. Why must the container be bonded and earthed?
options: To stop the container from rusting
To make the fuel drain faster
To stop static building up and sparking
To keep the container from being stolen

questions.stem: Which clothing is best for a fitter doing breakdown work in a hazardous area?
options: A nylon rain jacket over a cotton shirt
Flame-resistant, antistatic overalls
Shorts and a polyester T-shirt
Any clothes with no metal buttons

questions.stem: The team wants to use its engine-driven welder for a repair at a fuel terminal. Where must it be placed?
options: Next to the work, to keep the leads short
Inside the pump house, where it is out of the sun
Anywhere the truck can reach
Outside the hazardous area, as the permit says

questions.stem: Before welding a bracket in a classified area, which set of controls is normally needed?
options: Permit, gas test, fire watch, extinguisher, covered drains
A helmet, gloves and a bucket of water nearby
A sign saying 'Welding in progress' at each entrance
Good lighting and a dry floor only

questions.stem: During hot work at a fuel depot, what is the fire watch's duty?
options: To help the welder by holding the plates
To look out for fire and act at once
To fetch tools from the van
To fill in the welder's timesheet

questions.stem: Why are drains near a hot work site at a fuel depot covered with fire blankets or mats?
options: To stop rainwater cooling the weld
To stop tools and bolts falling into the drain
Vapour may be in drains, and sparks can fall in
To keep the work area looking tidy

questions.stem: Before a weld repair on a conveyor frame in a flour mill, what must be done about the dust?
options: Clean dust away and cover what cannot be moved
Spray lots of water to turn the dust into paste
Blow it away with compressed air
Nothing, as flour dust cannot burn

questions.stem: A breakdown repair needs a fitter to enter a fuel tank. Besides the hot work permit, what is needed?
options: Only a torch and a rope
A second welder working inside the tank with him
A ladder and a fan
A confined space permit, tests and an attendant

questions.stem: Why must a replacement motor for a pump in a Zone 1 area carry the right Ex marking?
options: So the motor runs at a higher speed
So that the motor can be bought much more cheaply
It shows the motor is safe for that zone and gas
So the motor needs no maintenance later

questions.stem: Steam pipes and hot engine exhausts are hazards in a classified area even when no one is welding. Why?
options: They make the area too noisy
A hot surface can ignite some gases
They make the gas heavier than air
They rust faster than other pipes

questions.stem: A site's rules call for non-sparking tools in a pump house. What is true about these tools?
options: They lower spark risk but do not replace gas tests
They make gas testing unnecessary
They let you grind without a permit
They are only ever needed for electrical work

questions.stem: A product pump at a terminal is down for 5 hours. Each hour stopped costs J$60 000 in lost transfers. What is the cost of the stoppage?
A permit allows hot work only while readings stay below 5% LEL. Which reading means the welder must stop?
options: 0% LEL
6% LEL
2% LEL
4% LEL

questions.stem: During a repair, the gas alarm sounds and the wind is blowing from the leak towards the team. What should they do?
options: Run straight downwind, away from the alarm
Finish the weld, then leave
Stop work and leave by the agreed route, upwind
Stay and look for the leak

questions.stem: Halfway through the job, the time on the hot work permit runs out. What should the team leader do?
options: Stop, make safe and get the permit renewed
Carry on working, as the job is nearly finished
Change the time on the permit himself
Ask the fire watch to sign an extension

questions.stem: A fuel line's flange gasket has just been renewed. Which steps must come before full flow is let back into the line?
options: Nothing, if the bolts look tight
Leak test, remove blinds, sign off the permit
Open the line fully at once to see if it leaks
Paint the flange so leaks will show

questions.stem: A pump at a fuel depot keeps losing its seal after only a few weeks. What should the team leader suggest?
options: Keep fitting new seals each time they fail
Tighten the gland more each time
Stop reporting the failures
Check alignment, bearings and the cause of failure

questions.stem: Why should the breakdown report record the gas test readings and the times they were taken?
options: It shows the work was done under safe conditions
It proves the detector's batteries were new
It tells the office how long lunch took
It means no permit will be needed next time

questions.stem: Before going to a breakdown at an LPG plant, why should the team leader find out what was in the line and how it was isolated?
options: To know how many hours the job will be paid for
To choose which van to take
To plan the right isolation, purging and tests
To decide who will drive back

questions.stem: A bracket must be fixed to a tank in a Zone 2 area. Which option avoids hot work?
options: Weld it with a small rod and low current
Braze it with a small gas torch
Grind it to fit, then tack it
Bolt it to an existing clamp or lug

questions.stem: Why is a welding habitat (a fire-resistant enclosure kept under positive pressure) sometimes used for hot work in a plant that must keep running?
options: To keep the welder cool in the hot sun all day
It keeps sparks in and outside gas out
To stop other workers watching
To save on welding gas

questions.stem: Which zone is used for a place where a combustible dust cloud is likely now and then in normal operation?
options: Zone 21
Zone 1
Zone 20
Zone 22

questions.stem: Methane at a sewage or biogas plant behaves differently from LPG. Where does methane tend to collect?
options: In drains and pits, low down
Evenly at all heights
High up, under roofs and covers
Only inside the pipework

questions.stem: Why should the team leader tell the plant's control room before starting and when finishing breakdown work?
options: So the control room staff can bill the client
So they can turn the lights off
So they can order lunch for the crew
So plant is not restarted and alarms are known

questions.stem: During a repair, the fitter notices a cracked cover on an Ex junction box near the pump. What should he do?
options: Report it at once; do not touch it himself
Tape the crack so gas cannot get in
Ignore it, as it is not part of his own job today
Open the box to check the wires inside

questions.stem: The LEL of a vapour is 1.2% by volume (given). A detector reads 50% LEL. What is the vapour concentration by volume?
Hot work at a fuel depot has finished for the day. What must happen before the permit is closed?
options: The welder leaves at once to beat the traffic
The tools are left in place for tomorrow
Fire watch done, area checked, permit signed off
The fire extinguishers are taken back to the van first

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A pump bay is in the gas zone where an explosive mixture is not expected in normal running and, if it ever forms, does not last long. Give the zone number.
Which gas, often used to purge flammable vapour out of pipework before hot work, can suffocate a person in an enclosed space?
The LEL of a gas is 2% by volume (given). A detector reads 25% LEL. What is the gas concentration, as a percentage by volume?
Two valves are shut on a fuel line and the small drain between them is left open, so any leak past the first valve is seen and vented. What is this arrangement called?
What is the solid steel plate called that is fitted between two flanges to positively shut off a pipe?
What word describes a person who has been trained and named in writing by the site to carry out or control work under a permit?
A hot work permit is valid from 8:00 a.m. for 6 hours. The weld repair is not finished by then. At what time must the work stop until the permit is renewed?
Before each day's use, the gas detector is briefly exposed to a known test gas to prove that its sensors and alarm work. What is this quick check called?
On a gas data sheet, what do the letters UEL stand for?
A 20 m length of pipe has a bore of 100 mm. The permit says to purge it with 5 times its volume of nitrogen. How many cubic metres of nitrogen is that, to two decimal places? (Use π = 3.142.)
Which gas, smelling of rotten eggs, can be found at sewage pumping stations and is toxic as well as flammable?
A small dust explosion shakes dust off beams into a cloud, which then explodes far more violently. What one word describes this second blast, as in a '______ explosion'?
Normal fresh air is about what percentage oxygen?
Which record, kept with the permit, shows each gas reading, the time it was taken and the name of the tester?
Before welding on a pipe that held fuel, it must be proved to hold no flammable vapour. What two words describe a pipe or vessel in this state?

essays.stem: A new fitter asks why the pump bay at a fuel depot, the bagging room at a sugar factory and the wet well at a sewage pumping station all need special rules for breakdown work. Explain the hazard at each, how zones are used to describe such places, and what this means for the work.
essays.modelAnswer: Each place can have a flammable atmosphere. At the fuel depot, fuel vapour from leaks, filling and drains can mix with air. At the sugar factory, fine sugar dust can form a cloud that explodes, and dust layers on beams can make a second, larger blast. In a sewage wet well, methane and hydrogen sulphide build up; hydrogen sulphide is also poisonous, and the well is a confined space. Sites show these risks on an area classification drawing. For gases, Zone 0 has an explosive mixture all or most of the time, Zone 1 has one now and then in normal work, and Zone 2 only rarely and briefly. Dust uses Zones 20, 21 and 22 in the same way. For the work, this means only authorised people work there under a permit; the air is tested before and during the job; tools, equipment and clothing must suit the zone; hot work needs extra controls such as a fire watch; and confined spaces need their own permit.
markingPoints: Names the hazard at each place (vapour, dust cloud, methane and hydrogen sulphide)
Gas zones 0, 1, 2 described in general terms
Dust zones 20, 21, 22 described in general terms
Only authorised people under a permit, with gas testing
Suitable equipment, hot work controls and confined space rules

essays.stem: A pipe support has broken in a Zone 1 area at a fuel terminal and must be repaired by welding. Describe the steps from receiving the call to handing the area back.
essays.modelAnswer: I would get the details: the location, the zone from the classification drawing, what is in the nearby lines and whether the pipe is safe meanwhile, for example by propping it. I would check whether a cold repair, such as a bolted clamp, would do; if welding is needed, it must be planned as hot work. With the site's operations staff, I would agree the isolation: the lines near the work are shut, drained, purged and blinded where needed, and nearby drains are covered. A permit to work and a hot work permit would be issued to my authorised team. A competent tester would bump test the detector and test the air at the work, low points and drains, before and during the work. Barriers, extinguishers, fire blankets and a fire watch would be in place, with the welder set up outside the zone. After the repair, the weld is inspected, the fire watch stays for the set time, the area is checked, isolations are removed under the permit, the permit is signed off and the report written.
markingPoints: Gathers details, checks the zone and makes the pipe safe meanwhile
Considers a cold repair before hot work
Isolation, draining, purging and blinding agreed with operations; permits issued to authorised people
Gas testing before and during; barriers, extinguishers, fire watch, welder outside the zone
Inspection, fire watch after, isolations removed, permit closed, report

essays.stem: A weld repair is to be done on a pipe bridge at a fuel terminal, close to a drain and a pump pit. Explain how you would plan the gas testing for the job and how the readings would control the work.
essays.modelAnswer: Gas testing must be done by a trained, authorised tester with a detector that has been calibrated within its date and bump tested that day. I would plan the test points: at the weld position, in and around the drain and the pump pit, which are low places where heavy vapour can collect, at any flanges or valves nearby, and downwind of the work. Tests would be done just before the permit is issued, again just before welding starts, and then at the times the permit sets, or continuously with a fixed or personal monitor during the work. Each reading, time and the tester's name would be written on the gas test record. If any reading is above the limit the permit allows, the work does not start; if readings rise during the work, the welding stops at once, equipment is made safe and the cause is found before the permit is reissued. A new test is also needed after any break.
markingPoints: Trained tester; detector calibrated and bump tested
Test points include the work, drain, pit, flanges and downwind
Tests before issue, before starting and during (or continuous)
Readings recorded with time and name
Clear rules: no start above the limit; stop at once if readings rise; retest after breaks

essays.stem: Explain how a fuel line is isolated, drained and purged before a weld repair, and why each step matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First, operations staff stop the flow and close the valves on each side of the section, using double block and bleed where the site requires it, and lock and tag them. Any pumps are isolated electrically and locked off. This stops fuel reaching the work. Next the section is drained into suitable containers that are bonded and earthed against static, and the fuel is taken away. This removes most of the fuel. Then the line is purged, usually with nitrogen or steam as the site procedure says, often with several times the pipe volume, to drive out the vapour. Where a positive break is needed, a spade or blind is fitted between flanges, because valves can leak. Finally the inside and the surroundings are gas tested to prove the line is gas free. Nitrogen is never replaced by oxygen or air from a cylinder, and the nitrogen itself is treated as a suffocation hazard. Every isolation is listed on the permit.
markingPoints: Valves closed (double block and bleed where required), locked and tagged; pumps isolated
Line drained safely, with containers bonded and earthed
Purged with nitrogen or steam as the procedure says
Blinds or spades for a positive break; gas test to prove gas free
Nitrogen treated as a suffocation hazard; isolations listed on the permit

essays.stem: Explain the duties of a fire watch for hot work in a hazardous area, and why the fire watch stays after the work ends.
essays.modelAnswer: The fire watch is a trained person whose only job during the hot work is to watch for fire. Before work starts, he checks that the area has been cleared of anything that can burn, that drains and gaps are covered, and that suitable extinguishers and fire blankets are ready and that he knows how to use them and raise the alarm. During the work he watches where sparks and hot slag land, including below gratings and behind walls, and keeps people away. He stops the work if he sees fire, smoke, a gas alarm or anything unsafe, and puts out small fires if it is safe to do so. He does not weld, fetch tools or leave his post. After the work ends he stays for the time the permit sets, because smouldering material, hot slag or a hidden spark can start a fire some time later. He then checks the area again and signs the permit.
markingPoints: Trained person with no other task during the hot work
Checks the area, covers and extinguishers before work starts
Watches sparks and slag, keeps people away, stops work if unsafe, fights small fires
Stays for the set time afterwards because smouldering can ignite later
Final check and signs the permit

essays.stem: Compare hot work and cold work methods for a breakdown repair in a hazardous area. Explain when you would choose each, and the controls each needs.
essays.modelAnswer: Hot work is any work that makes flames, sparks or hot surfaces: welding, gas cutting, brazing and grinding. Cold work does not: bolting, using clamps, hand sawing, cold cutting machines and replacing parts. In a hazardous area, cold methods should be chosen first wherever they will give a safe, lasting repair, such as a bolted clamp on a pipe support or a bolted bracket on a tank lug, if the engineer approves. Hot work is chosen only when there is no safe cold method, for example when a structural support must be restored to full strength. Cold work still needs a permit, isolation where parts are opened, gas testing and suitable tools, because even dropped steel tools or static can make a spark. Hot work needs much more: a hot work permit, the area made gas free with isolations and purging, gas testing before and during, cleared and covered surroundings, extinguishers, a fire watch during and after, and the welding set outside the zone.
markingPoints: Defines hot work and cold work with examples
Cold methods first where they give a safe, lasting repair
Hot work only when no safe cold method exists
Controls for cold work (permit, isolation, gas test, suitable tools)
Extra controls for hot work (gas free, continuous testing, covers, extinguishers, fire watch, set outside zone)

essays.stem: At a fuel terminal, the operations supervisor issues the permit and you lead the repair crew. Describe what each of you is responsible for under the permit, from issue to sign-off.
essays.modelAnswer: The operations supervisor, as the permit issuer, is responsible for the plant side: making sure the equipment is isolated, drained, purged and blinded as needed, arranging the gas test, stating the hazards, the controls and the time limit on the permit, and signing it only when it is safe. As the crew leader, I accept the permit, check on site that the isolations and controls listed are really in place, and sign to accept it. I brief my crew on the permit, the hazards and the emergency plan, and make sure only authorised, trained people do the work, within the stated scope, place and time. If the job changes, conditions change, the time runs out or the gas alarm sounds, I stop the work and go back to the issuer. When the work is finished I make sure the area is clean, the fire watch has done its time and my crew are clear, then I hand the permit back. The issuer checks the area, removes isolations and closes the permit.
markingPoints: Issuer: isolations, gas test, hazards, controls and time on the permit
Crew leader: checks controls on site and accepts the permit
Crew leader: briefs the crew and keeps work within scope, place and time
Stops work and returns to the issuer if anything changes
Hand-back: area clean, fire watch done, crew clear; issuer removes isolations and closes

essays.stem: A conveyor frame in a sugar factory's bagging area has cracked and must be weld-repaired. Describe how you would control the dust hazard before, during and after the repair.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the repair, I would check the area classification and get a permit and a hot work permit. The conveyor and nearby plant would be stopped and isolated so no fresh dust is made. All dust layers on the frame, beams, floor and nearby ledges would be cleaned away with suitable vacuum equipment or wet methods, never blown with compressed air, which makes a dust cloud. Anything that cannot be moved would be covered with fire blankets, and openings to ducts and hoppers sealed. Extinguishers would be ready and a fire watch posted. During the repair I would keep the work area small, screen sparks, and stop if dust starts to build up or the fire watch sees smouldering. After the repair the fire watch stays for the set time, the area is checked for hot spots and smouldering dust, cleaned again, and the permit closed. I would report how the dust built up so housekeeping can be improved.
markingPoints: Permit and hot work permit; plant stopped and isolated
Dust layers removed by vacuum or wet methods, never compressed air
Covers, sealed openings, extinguishers and fire watch
Small, screened work area; stop if dust builds or smouldering seen
Fire watch after, recheck and clean, close the permit and report housekeeping problems

essays.stem: During a repair, the plant manager pushes you to start welding before the gas test results are in, because the plant is losing money. Explain what you would do and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I would politely but firmly refuse to start the hot work until the gas test has been done, the readings are within the permit limit and the permit has been issued and signed. I would explain that the area may contain vapour that cannot be seen or smelt, and that a weld arc or spark could cause a fire or explosion that would injure or kill people and stop the plant for far longer. The permit system exists to protect everyone, including the manager, and nobody, however senior, may skip a step. While the test is being done, I would use the time well: set up barriers, extinguishers and covers, brief the crew and prepare the parts, so welding can start as soon as it is safe. I would record the pressure in my report and, if it continued, tell my own manager. Production losses can be recovered; lives cannot.
markingPoints: Refuses to start until the gas test is done and the permit issued
Explains the danger of unseen vapour and ignition
Explains that no one may bypass the permit system
Uses the waiting time to prepare so work can start promptly
Records the pressure and reports it if it continues

essays.stem: After a breakdown repair in a hazardous area, describe how you would return the plant to service and what you would write in the breakdown report, saying why each record matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would inspect the repair: the weld or bolted joint, gaskets and fixings, and any Ex equipment disturbed, checking nothing is left open or loose. The area would be cleared of tools, rags and waste, and the fire watch would complete the set time after any hot work. Under the permit, the operations staff would remove blinds, open valves and restore isolations in order, and the line would be leak tested before full flow. Only then would the permit be signed off and the plant handed back to the control room. In the report I would record the fault and its cause, so repeat failures can be spotted; the repair method and parts used, with any Ex details, so the equipment register stays correct; the permits, isolations and gas test readings with times, as proof the work was done safely; the tests done after the repair; the downtime, for cost records; and any recommendations, such as a better pump seal or more frequent checks, so the problem does not return.
markingPoints: Inspects the repair and the area; fire watch completes its time
Isolations removed in order under the permit; leak test before full flow
Permit signed off and plant handed back to the control room
Report: cause, repair, parts with Ex details, permits, gas readings, tests, downtime
Explains why each record matters and gives recommendations

practical1.title: Plan the response to a fuel line breakdown that needs a weld repair (paper exercise with permits)
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a breakdown scenario at a fuel terminal: a cracked weld on a pipe support beside a fuel line in a Zone 1 area, with a site plan showing the zones, valves, drains and the pump pit. As the breakdown team, plan the whole response on paper. Share the roles: team leader (job plan, sequence and crew roles; decides whether a cold repair is possible), isolation lead (isolation, draining, purging and blind plan, marked in colour on the site plan, with the purge volume worked out), gas test lead (test points marked on the plan, test times and the stop rules), hot work lead (draft hot work permit, fire watch plan, covers, extinguishers and where the welding set goes) and records lead (gas test record sheet and a blank breakdown report ready to fill in). In a group of four, the team leader also does the records. Each member signs their own part. Finish with a five-minute toolbox briefing, given by the team leader with each member presenting their part, while the assessor plays the permit issuer and asks questions. Photograph each part.
materials: Scenario card and site plan with zones, valves, drains and pit (from the assessor)
Blank permit to work, hot work permit, gas test record and breakdown report templates
Data sheet with the pipe size, the purge rule and the gas details (from the assessor)
A portable gas detector, if the Centre has one, to show the bump test
photos: The site plan marked with zones, isolation points and blinds
The gas test points and schedule on the plan
The completed draft hot work permit and fire watch plan
The purge volume and other workings
The gas test record and breakdown report templates ready
The toolbox briefing, with the assessor as permit issuer
checklist: Read the site plan and zones correctly
Considered a cold repair before choosing hot work, with a reason
Planned a complete isolation, drain, purge and blind sequence
Placed gas test points sensibly (work, low points, drains, downwind) and set clear stop rules
Listed hot work controls: permit, gas test, covers, extinguishers, fire watch during and after, set outside the zone
Worked out the purge volume correctly
Presented their part clearly and answered the issuer's questions
safety: This is a paper exercise: no gas, fuel or flame is used
If a gas detector is shown, only the instructor operates the test gas, following the maker's instructions
Treat the plan as real: every hazard needs a control
Keep the room tidy and speak respectfully during the briefing

practical2.title: Simulated hot work repair in a marked 'hazardous area': permit, gas test, fire watch and weld repair of a bracket
practical2.brief: The assessor marks out a mock 'Zone 2' area in the welding shop with tape and signs, around a pipe-support mock-up with a cracked or broken bracket. No fuel or flammable gas is present; everything else is done as it would be on a real site. The assessor acts as the permit issuer and gives gas readings on cards (or uses the Centre's detector on clean air). The group must: (1) request and accept the permit and the hot work permit, checking every control listed; (2) carry out the 'gas tests' at the points the permit names, record them and decide whether to start; (3) set up the area: barriers and signs, drain cover (fire blanket), cleared combustibles, extinguishers and screens, with the welding set outside the marked area; (4) prepare and weld the repair to the bracket while one member acts as fire watch and another repeats the gas test at the set times; (5) when the assessor hands in a 'rising reading' card, stop at once and make safe, then restart only when the assessor reissues the permit; (6) inspect the weld, keep the fire watch for the time the assessor sets, clean up, hand back and sign off the permit, and fill in the breakdown report. Rotate the roles so every member welds or prepares part of the repair, and acts at least once as fire watch or gas tester.
materials: Pipe-support mock-up with a cracked or broken bracket, and replacement flat bar
Tape, signs and barriers to mark the area
Fire blankets, two suitable extinguishers and welding screens

checklist: Checked the permit's listed controls on site before accepting it
Did or recorded gas tests at the right points and times, and applied the stop rule
Set up barriers, covers, extinguishers and screens, with the set outside the area
Prepared and welded the repair to a sound standard, wearing full PPE
As fire watch, stayed at post, watched sparks and slag and did not do other tasks
Stopped at once and made safe when the reading rose; restarted only on reissue
Kept the fire watch for the set time, cleaned up and signed off the permit
safety: No fuel, flammable gas or flammable liquid is to be brought into the exercise
Weld only behind screens, with full PPE, and treat the repaired bracket as hot
Keep an extinguisher and fire blanket within reach throughout
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for the welding set and the detector
